correctness.rationale: Three moment constraints amount to target (1/2,1/3) in convex hull of parabola Γ(t)=(t,t²); interior membership is equivalent to strictly positive weights for every node by mixing with the mean node vector. At mean 1/2, chord of 1/2−u and 1/2+v has second moment 1/4+uv. Hence straddling and l r<1/12<L R, where l,r are nearest and L,R extreme distances, is exact a.s. Joint extreme and nearest densities are m(m−1)(u+v)^{m−2} and m(m−1)(1−u−v)^{m−2}, respectively; integrating their disjoint failure events yields the formula. Laurent polynomial integration makes p_m rational + rational log3. Endpoint Laplace at u=1/6 and 1/2 contributes (1/2+3/2)(2/3)^m; the explicit (2/3)^m adds 1, giving coefficient3 while the nearest contribution decays strictly faster. Direct exact series bounds put p10=.9411269334<.95 and p11=.9603356140>.95; monotonicity gives sharp first cutoff. Independent numerical integration, finite endpoint-ratio checks and Monte Carlo at m4,7,10 agree; these do not prove asymptotics.

final_claim: For m≥2 iid uniform [0,1] nodes, the exact probability of strictly positive weights on every node integrating 1,t,t² is 1−(2/3)^m+(1/3)^m−m∫_{1/6}^{1/2}[(u+1/(12u))^{m−1}+(1−u−1/(12u))^{m−1}]du; the failure probability is asymptotic to 3(2/3)^m and the first m with p_m≥.95 is 11.
limitations: Uniform iid [0,1] nodes, quadratic monomials, unrestricted strictly positive weights only; no near-equal weight bounds or higher degree.
Tail asymptotic is analytic, not a conclusion from finite-m tail ratios.
